description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05) while recording the `Contract:` docstring tails
for the numeric family (Part B item B1, task #1170).  PRE-EXISTING; found by
probe, not by a runner.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bm/p-contract.pl):

    my $v = eval { 5 % 0 };
    print defined $v ? "[$v]" : "undef", " err=[$@]\n";

  perl 5.40.3   undef  err=[Illegal modulus zero at FILE line 2.]
  PCL           [NaN]  err=[]

THE CAUSE is one arm of `%p-%-slow` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: it folds
`(zerop nb)` in with NaN and the two infinities and returns a quiet NaN
double.  The fast path `p-%` guards `(not (eql b 0))` and hands 0 to the slow
path, so both routes reach that arm.

    (if (or (%pcl-nan-p na) (%pcl-nan-p nb)
            (and (floatp na) (sb-ext:float-infinity-p na))
            (and (floatp nb) (sb-ext:float-infinity-p nb))
            (zerop nb))
        (sb-kernel:make-double-float #x7FF80000 0)      ; <- quiet NaN
        (mod (truncate na) (truncate nb)))

perl's `pp_modulo` dies on a zero right operand.  The NaN answers for the
OTHER three conditions were NOT probed here -- measure each against perl
before touching them; only the zero case is claimed by this task, and it must
become a trappable perl-shaped `(p-die "Illegal modulus zero")`, like `p-/`'s.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond the message: NaN is a VALUE the program then consumes,
so this is rule-12's die-not-fall-through case in its worst form -- the
archetype the rule was written for.  `$x % $n` with a computed `$n` that
happens to be 0 gives a plausible-looking NaN that propagates.

`p-%`'s docstring now carries `Contract: ... dies=yes ...` (ir-spec §10a: the
tail states the op's PERL contract, and a divergence from it is a bug, which
is this task).

BAR: the reproducer above; the perl-shaped message and location; `$x %= 0`
(the compound twin, which reaches the same slow path -- probe it); the gate;
the full sweep (a `cl/` change is invisible to corpus-diff) and the op/
companion leg.  Check whether any blessed baseline row was PASSING on the NaN.

=== TWO MORE CONTRACT DIVERGENCES, same probe run, same class (s470bm) ===
Both found while recording the `Contract:` tails for the string and element
families; both PRE-EXISTING; the same fix shape (make the op meet the contract
the inventory now states).

(a) `substr($s, OFFSET)` PAST THE END.
      perl 5.40.3   substr("abc", 10, 2)  ->  undef, and SILENT with no
                    `use warnings`
      PCL           ->  "" (a defined empty string), and it prints
                    `substr outside of string` on stderr UNCONDITIONALLY
    Two divergences in one: the VALUE (undef vs ""), which a `defined()` test
    sees, and an unconditional diagnostic where perl gates on warnings
    (the #221 family).

(b) `exists $s->{k}` ON A NON-REF SCALAR.
      perl 5.40.3   ""     (defined false)
      PCL           undef
    Both are false, so only `defined` tells them apart â but that is exactly
    the `$&`-family rule of #416 (a false answer from a builtin is a DEFINED
    empty string, never undef), so it is the same rule already settled
    elsewhere.

Reproducer for both: scratch/s470bm/p-contract.pl in the s470bm worktree, or
rewrite it â three lines each.

=== DONE (s470bo) â all three items ===

(1) `5 % 0` NOW DIES.  The NaN arm's `(zerop nb)` disjunct is gone; the modulo
body dies `Illegal modulus zero`, trappable by eval as perl's is.

ONE BODY, NOT TWO (rule 11).  `p-%=` spelled its arithmetic out again inline â
`(mod (truncate (to-number c)) (truncate (to-number d)))` â which is exactly
how `$x %= 0` came to raise a RAW CL error while `$x % 0` answered NaN.  Both
now call the new `%p-modulo`, which is also `%p-%-slow`'s fallback.

The zero test is on the TRUNCATED right operand, because that is perl's:
probed, `5 % 0.5` and `5 % 0.9` BOTH die.  (`/` differs â see #1174.)

THE OTHER THREE CONDITIONS WERE MEASURED, as this task asked.  Two are perl's
(a NaN operand, an infinite LEFT operand); the third is WRONG and is filed as
**#1191** â `5 % inf` is 5 in perl, `-5 % inf` is Inf (the mathematical modulo,
carrying the sign of the right operand), and PCL answers NaN for all four
sign combinations.  Deliberately left alone: it is a value, not a die, and its
fix has to compute a float modulo rather than answer a constant.

(2) `substr($s, OFFSET)` PAST THE END now returns undef.  An out-of-range READ
returns `*p-undef*`; the in-range one-past-the-end position (`substr("abc",3)`)
still returns "", as perl does.  Probed all seven offset/length shapes.
The unconditional "substr outside of string" diagnostic STAYS â perl gates it
on `use warnings`, which is #221 â and the guard row isolates the value claim
with a `$SIG{__WARN__}` sink rather than blessing the diagnostic into an
expected string.

(3) A FALSE `exists` is now the DEFINED empty string.  This was the whole
family, not just the non-ref case the task named: each of `p-exists`,
`p-exists-array`, `p-sub-exists` and `p-coderef-exists-p` returned a CL
boolean (or a box holding nil), so EVERY false `exists` was undef.  All four
now wrap the existing `p-bool` (rule 11 â it was already there, one screen up
from the numeric compares), with the CL-boolean bodies split out so the
perl-value conversion is stated once per op.  Probed five false forms (hash
miss, aryref out of range, `exists &nope`, `%ENV` miss, non-ref scalar) and
three true ones, all identical to perl.  Nothing in `cl/**` calls these in CL
boolean position â checked â and every generated consumer goes through
`p-true-p`.

BARS: gate 208 files / 7035 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows; targeted sweep
over arith/arith2/array/delete/exists_sub/hash/substr/int/bop
before and after = TOTAL 1290 passing / 54 failing, IDENTICAL, so no blessed
row moved; companion `--jobs 1` over op/inc.t opbasic/arith.t op/int.t
op/substr.t op/exists_sub.t op/delete.t before and after = identical verdicts
and counts.  Six run rows in `Pl/t/census-bugs-01.t`.
subject: `5 % 0` answers NaN where perl DIES "Illegal modulus zero" - a silent wrong in p-%
